blocks.text: Good morning Tiffany,

Following on from the message below, we now have the complete file history and the USPTO assignment record for each family on the licensor's schedule, and each family's next official deadline is entered on our docket so that nothing in the portfolio lapses unnoticed while the license terms are being worked out. The reading itself starts with the chain of title, because the rest of the review assumes the licensor owns what it proposes to license.

To move from collecting the record to reading it, we need the following:
1. The signed inventor assignments, or the employment agreements relied on in their place, for any family where the recorded chain does not run from every named inventor to the licensor. We can request these from the licensor's counsel directly if you would rather not relay them.
2. An editable copy of the patent schedule attached to the draft license, so that we can mark it up family by family.
3. A product description or data sheet for what {{fact:f:E-2025-001.client}} intends to make or sell under the license, since that decides which claims we read against the product first.

Where the record shows a gap or an encumbrance, I will set out what the documents say and leave the question of what it means for the license to counsel, who will give you that view in writing once the record is complete.
Sincerely,
Minutes of Working Session: Licensing Diligence for {{fact:f:E-2025-001.client}}
Privileged and Confidential. Attorney-Client Communication.
Attendees

The session took {{fact:f:E-2025-001.client}} through the results of the title and status review, which is complete for the United States families, and settled the order of the claim review that follows. Items are recorded in the order taken.
Matters Discussed

1. Chain of title. David Chang reported that the recorded chain runs from the inventors to the licensor for every family except one, in which a single inventor's assignment was never recorded. The licensor has produced that inventor's employment agreement, which uses present-tense assignment language, and Mary Bradley's preliminary view is that the agreement probably carries title; she nonetheless recommended a confirmatory assignment, executed and recorded before signing, so that the point does not rest on the agreement's wording.

2. Status. Every issued patent on the schedule is in force, and no pending application has a response overdue. Richard Henderson noted that one continuation in the mechanical group was allowed over a terminal disclaimer tying it to its parent, which leaves the continuation enforceable only while the two remain commonly owned, and that the draft schedule lists only the parent.

3. Security interest. The assignment record shows a security interest in favor of a lender against part of the portfolio, with no release of record. Tiffany Munoz asked whether this prevents the license from being signed; Mary Bradley answered that it does not necessarily, but that the lender's rights and any consent requirement must be understood first, and that a recorded release or the lender's written consent is the cleaner course.

4. Maintenance fees. Tiffany Munoz asked who will carry the maintenance fees that fall due during the license term and what they will amount to. David Chang will prepare a schedule of the upcoming fee windows by family from the docket, with the official fee for each, so that the allocation can be negotiated against actual amounts.

5. Claim review. The claim review begins with the firmware and control families, which David Chang will read against the product description {{fact:f:E-2025-001.client}} supplied, and continues with the mechanical families under Richard Henderson. Mary Bradley asked that the readings be presented as findings and not as opinions on infringement or validity; any opinion will be given separately, in writing, if {{fact:f:E-2025-001.client}} requests one. Tiffany Munoz confirmed that the product description already supplied is current and that she will tell the team if the design changes while the review is under way.

6. Foreign counterparts. The schedule lists foreign counterparts for several families, and the licensor handles their prosecution through its own foreign associates, so their status can be confirmed only from records the licensor holds. That work follows the United States review and will be reported in its own section of the findings memorandum.
Actions Agreed

rows: Write to the licensor's counsel requesting a confirmatory assignment for the unrecorded inventor, either a release from the lender or its written consent to the license, and the foreign file records for the scheduled counterparts.
Prepare the maintenance fee schedule by family from the docket and send it to Tiffany Munoz.
Begin the claim reading on the firmware and control families against the product description.
Mark up the draft patent schedule to add the terminally disclaimed continuation beside its parent, then begin the mechanical family reading.
Confirm whether {{fact:f:E-2025-001.client}} wants the security interest resolved before signing or addressed in the license terms.

blocks.text: The next step is Mary Bradley's letter to the licensor's counsel on the unrecorded assignment and the security interest.
Status Report: Licensing Diligence for {{fact:f:E-2025-001.client}}
Prepared for {{fact:f:E-2025-001.client}} by David Chang, Patent Agent, with Richard Henderson, Patent Agent, and Mary Bradley, Managing Partner. Privileged and confidential.
Where the Review Stands

The review is at roughly its halfway point and on schedule. Title and status work on the United States families is finished, the encumbrance search is finished, and the claim reading is complete in draft for the firmware and control families and under way for the mechanical families.

Two items from the working session remain open on the licensor's side: the confirmatory assignment for the unrecorded inventor, and a release or consent covering the recorded security interest. Neither has held up the claim reading, but both need to be resolved, or dealt with in the license terms, before signing.
Completed to Date

rows: The recorded chain runs from the inventors to the licensor for every family but one. The licensor has produced the employment agreement for the unrecorded inventor, and a confirmatory assignment has been requested through its counsel.
Issued patents are in force and no pending application has a response overdue. The maintenance fee schedule by family was sent to {{fact:f:E-2025-001.client}} after the working session.
One recorded security interest in favor of the licensor's lender, with no release of record. No recorded licenses or other liens against the scheduled families were found.
The terminally disclaimed continuation has been added to the marked-up patent schedule beside its parent.
Claim reading, firmware and control families
Read against the product description {{fact:f:E-2025-001.client}} supplied. The draft is with Mary Bradley for review.
Richard Henderson is reading the independent claims against the housing and mounting drawings in the product description.

blocks.text: The firmware and control reading compares each independent claim, element by element, with how the product description says the control board and its firmware behave. Where an element turns on behavior the description does not cover, such as how the firmware responds to a sensor fault or a power interruption, the reading marks the element open instead of assuming an answer.

A short call with whoever at {{fact:f:E-2025-001.client}} knows the firmware best would close most of those open elements. I can send the list of questions ahead of the call so it takes less of their time.

The mechanical reading follows the same method, with the drawings in the product description standing in for the product itself. One mechanical family's claims were amended during prosecution, and whether that amendment confines them to an arrangement the product does not use will be settled in the prosecution history review, not from the claim text alone.
Work Ahead

Before the findings memorandum, in this order:
1. Finish the mechanical family reading, starting with the families closest to the planned product.
2. Review the prosecution history of each family the readings rely on, for amendments or arguments that narrow what its claims can cover.
3. Confirm the status of the foreign counterparts. The schedule lists them, but the licensor has not yet supplied the foreign file records.
4. Prepare the findings memorandum, family by family, for Mary Bradley's review. Any statement about what {{fact:f:E-2025-001.client}} can or cannot rely on in the license will come from her and not from the claim readings.
Risks and Open Items

1. Security interest. Until a release or the lender's consent is of record, the lender's rights in part of the portfolio are not fully known. If neither arrives before signing, Mary Bradley will advise on how the license terms should address it.
2. Confirmatory assignment. The employment agreement may well be sufficient on its own, but a recorded confirmatory assignment removes the question. The licensor has not said when it will sign.
3. Foreign records. The foreign counterpart review depends on records the licensor holds through its own foreign associates. A delay there would hold up that part of the review but not the United States findings.
4. Schedule changes. If the licensor adds families to the schedule, review of those families falls outside the current scope, and we would raise it with you before doing the work.
Budget

The engagement is being performed for the fixed fee of {{fact:f:E-2025-001.fee}}. Work to date is within that fee, and nothing now planned calls for a change to it. Additional families, or a request for a formal opinion beyond the findings memorandum, would be scoped and agreed with you separately before any work starts.
Questions on the claim readings can come to me. Questions on the open title items or on the license terms should go to Mary Bradley, who will also review the findings memorandum before it is sent.
Review of Draft Findings: Licensing Diligence for {{fact:f:E-2025-001.client}}
Privileged and confidential. These minutes record legal advice given to {{fact:f:E-2025-001.client}} and should not be circulated outside its management.
Present

The session reviewed the draft findings memorandum, which was circulated to {{fact:f:E-2025-001.client}} beforehand, and the title items still open with the licensor. Points are grouped below by subject rather than in the order raised.
Firmware and Control Families

David Chang summarized the readings. On the product description {{fact:f:E-2025-001.client}} supplied, and with most of the open claim elements closed in the call with its engineering staff, the independent claims of these families appear to read on the control board and its firmware as described. Mary Bradley repeated that the memorandum states findings and is not an opinion on infringement or validity, and that each finding carries the qualifications the record requires.
Mechanical Families

Richard Henderson reported that the claims of one mechanical family were narrowed during prosecution by an amendment limiting them to a mounting arrangement the planned product does not use, so on the present design that family is unlikely to cover the product, although a design change could alter the answer. Tiffany Munoz asked whether the family should remain in the royalty base. Mary Bradley said that is a commercial decision for {{fact:f:E-2025-001.client}}, and that the firm can draft schedule language that either removes the family or prices it separately.
Title

The confirmatory assignment for the previously unrecorded inventor has been executed and recorded, and the assignment record now shows a complete chain for every family. The licensor reports that the lender's release has been filed, but it does not yet appear on the assignment record. Mary Bradley noted that a gap between filing and recordation is common and is usually a matter of processing, but that the memorandum should not describe the portfolio as unencumbered until the record shows the release.
Foreign Counterparts

David Chang reported that the licensor's foreign associates have now supplied the foreign file records, and that each counterpart on the schedule is either pending or in force in the jurisdiction the schedule shows. The memorandum treats the counterparts in a separate section and says expressly that it relies on the associates' reports for local status, which the firm has not independently verified.
Carrying the Findings into the License

Tiffany Munoz asked which findings should be reflected in the license itself. Mary Bradley recommended three provisions: a representation by the licensor that title to the scheduled patents is complete and unencumbered; a covenant to keep the scheduled patents in force under the maintenance fee allocation now being negotiated; and a condition that the lender's release be of record before signing.
Actions

items: David Chang: check the assignment record each business day for the lender's release and notify the team when it posts.
Richard Henderson: add the prosecution history note on the narrowed mechanical family to the memorandum, citing the amendment and the examiner's reasons for allowance.
Mary Bradley: send Tiffany Munoz proposed license language on title, maintenance, and the release condition.
Tiffany Munoz: decide whether the narrowed mechanical family stays in the royalty base, and tell Mary Bradley.

blocks.text: Once the release appears on the assignment record, the findings memorandum issues in final; that is the next step.
